newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania Socialists want emergency end before vote.
newsitem.headline: Albania Socialists want emergency end before vote.

text.p: Albania's Socialist Party, main rival to President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party, demanded on Tuesday that a state of emergency imposed during March riots be lifted before June 29 elections.
"To have free and fair elections we must lift the state of the emergency law," said Et'hem Ruka, a Socialist leader.

Ruka said the state of emergency, declared at the height of rioting and looting sparked by the failure of shady pyramid investment schemes, caused widespread feelings of insecurity among the public and gave the Democratic Party an unfair advantage.

"Under the state of emergency, the Interior Minister (of the Democratic Party) has the main prerogatives to intervene and this means the Interior Ministry could have more power than the national reconciliation government," Ruka said.

At the weekend, Albanian television quoted Berisha as saying it was no longer within his power to end the state of emergency, which includes a 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. curfew, because only Parliament has authority to do so and it has been dissolved.

Ruka spoke to reporters as his party and most other political parties held talks convened by the Democratic Party to discuss adopting a "social contract" which would bind all the parties to abide by the results of the June 29 elections.
A draft text of the contract said that signatories "agree that parliamentary elections on June 29 are indispensable to come out of the crisis and return normality to the country.

"Violence for political reasons especially with weapons is condemnable by all. ... We call on the national reconciliation government to fully reestablish law and public order and bring back to full efficiency the local goverment structures," the draft added.
